s1.syndrome_frame: Persistent painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition on the hand following a twisting injury
salient_findings: Painful bruise on the hand that persisted despite icing and resting
Ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque on the dorsum of the left hand
Heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion on Magnetic Resonance Imaging
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 30s
The patient sustained a twisting injury to the affected hand while participating in acroyoga 2 years prior
The bruise and pain initially appeared a few days after the injury
The patient denied any personal or family history of bleeding disorders
Radiography showed soft tissue swelling but were otherwise unremarkable
Magnetic Resonance Imaging showed a heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion
Pathology showed mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli
Immunohistochemistry was strongly positive for CD34 and negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A

shortlist.label: Nora lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition on the hand

shortlist.label: Spindle cell lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with pathology findings of spindled cells and mature adipose tissue

shortlist.label: Angiolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the presence of soft tissue swelling and mixed fibrous and adipose tissue

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the presence of spindled and epithelioid cells with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli

shortlist.label: Atypical lipomatous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Included due to the large size of the lesion and the presence of mixed inflammatory infiltrate

raw.rationale: The presence of a painful bruise, mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition, and lesional cells that are spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli, along with strong positivity for CD34, are consistent with a Nora lesion, a rare benign lesion that typically presents as a painful subcutaneous nodule

rejected.label: Spindle cell lipoma
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic floret-like cells and absence of S100 positivity

rejected.label: Pleomorphic lipoma
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic floret-like cells and absence of S100 positivity

rejected.label: Atypical lipomatous tumor
rejected.why: Absence of characteristic atypical cells and MDM2 amplification
